eic.name: English East India Company
eic.summary: A London joint-stock company chartered in 1600 to trade in Asia. By 1765 it collected the land revenue of Bengal and Bihar and kept its own army.

eic-diwani.name: Bengal under Company diwani
eic-diwani.summary: After 1765 the Company held the diwani (the right to collect revenue) for Bengal, Bihar and Orissa. The Nawab kept the nizamat (justice and policing) in name only. Historians call this arrangement the "dual government".

bengal-nawabs.name: Nawabs of Bengal
bengal-nawabs.summary: The Mughal province of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa. It was in practice independent under nawabs based at Murshidabad, and it was the richest province of the empire.

awadh.name: Nawabs of Awadh
awadh.summary: A Mughal successor state in the middle Ganges plain. Shuja-ud-Daula ruled from 1754, and his defeat at Buxar made Awadh a buffer state of the Company.

mughal.name: Mughal Empire
mughal.summary: By the 1740s the emperor in Delhi was sovereign in name, but his real power reached little beyond the capital region. Provincial governors and rival powers held the rest.

maratha-peshwa.name: Maratha Confederacy (Peshwa)
maratha-peshwa.summary: A confederacy based at Pune under the Peshwas. In the 1750s it was the strongest power on the subcontinent, until its defeat at Panipat in 1761.

marathas-nagpur.name: Bhonsles of Nagpur
marathas-nagpur.summary: A Maratha house based at Nagpur. Its armies raided Bengal from 1741, and in 1751 it took Orissa from the Nawab of Bengal.

rohillas.name: Rohillas
rohillas.summary: Afghan chiefs who took control of Rohilkhand, north-west of Awadh, in the 1740s.

hyderabad.name: Nizams of Hyderabad
hyderabad.summary: A Mughal successor state in the Deccan, independent in practice from 1724.

mysore.name: Kingdom of Mysore
mysore.summary: A Wodeyar kingdom in the southern Deccan. From 1761 the commander Haidar Ali held real power.

carnatic.name: Nawabs of the Carnatic (Arcot)
carnatic.summary: A Mughal successor state on the Coromandel coast. Rival claimants backed by the British and the French fought for it in the Carnatic Wars.

travancore.name: Travancore
travancore.summary: A kingdom in the far south-west, enlarged by Marthanda Varma in the 1740s.

french.name: French East India Company
french.summary: The main European rival of the British in the 1740s–1750s. Its headquarters was Pondicherry.

dutch.name: Dutch East India Company (VOC)
dutch.summary: The VOC, once the leading European trader in Asia. Its Bengal base was Chinsurah.

danish.name: Danish East India Company
danish.summary: A small Danish trading presence at Tranquebar (from 1620) and Serampore (from 1755).

portuguese.name: Portuguese Estado da Índia
portuguese.summary: The first European power in India. By the 18th century it held only Goa, Daman and Diu.

keyframes.note: Starting state. Alivardi Khan takes Bengal after Giria. The Bhonsles of Nagpur hold Nagpur and are advancing into Chhattisgarh.
After ten years of Maratha raids, Alivardi Khan cedes Orissa to the Bhonsles and agrees to pay chauth (a tribute) for Bengal. Midnapore stays with Bengal.
After Plassey, Mir Jafar grants the Company the zamindari (the right to hold land and collect its revenue) of the 24 Parganas, south of Calcutta.
Mir Qasim takes the throne and pays the Company with Burdwan, Midnapore and Chittagong. Chittagong is in present-day Bangladesh, and it is not yet in the base map.

Treaty of Allahabad. Shah Alam II grants the Company the diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa. Awadh gives Allahabad and Kora to the emperor. The Chingleput jagir is also shown, granted to the Company by the Nawab of Arcot in 1763.

places.name: Calcutta
places.why: The Company's Bengal base. Siraj-ud-Daulah captured it in 1756 and renamed it Alinagar; Clive retook it in 1757. It later became the capital of British India (until 1911).

places.name: Murshidabad
places.why: Capital of the Nawabs of Bengal. Siraj-ud-Daulah was executed here, and Clive installed Mir Jafar here.

places.name: Plassey
places.why: The site of the 1757 battle that gave the Company control over the Nawab of Bengal. It was decided more by defection than by fighting.

places.name: Kasimbazar
places.why: A silk-trade centre beside Murshidabad, with Company, Dutch and French factories. Siraj-ud-Daulah seized the English factory in June 1756.

control.note: Restored under the Treaty of Alinagar

places.name: Chandernagore
places.why: The French base in Bengal, captured by Clive and Watson in March 1757.

control.note: Restored after the Treaty of Paris (1763)

places.name: Chinsurah
places.why: The Dutch base in Bengal. The British defeated a Dutch force nearby at Chinsurah (Bedara) in 1759.

places.name: Frederiksnagore
places.why: A Danish settlement on the Hooghly, founded in 1755.

places.name: Fulta
places.why: Where Company refugees from Calcutta sheltered on ships in 1756, until Clive arrived.

places.name: Patna
places.why: The main city of Bihar and a centre of the saltpetre trade. Fighting between Mir Qasim and the Company began here in 1763.

places.name: Giria
places.why: Where Alivardi Khan defeated Nawab Sarfaraz Khan and took Bengal in 1740.

places.name: Udhwa Nala
places.why: Where the Company defeated Mir Qasim in 1763.

places.name: Manihari
places.why: Where Siraj-ud-Daulah defeated his rival cousin Shaukat Jang of Purnea in 1756.

places.name: Buxar
places.why: Site of the 1764 battle in which the Company defeated the combined armies of Mir Qasim, Awadh and the Mughal emperor. Many historians rank it as more decisive than Plassey.

places.name: Allahabad
places.why: Where Shah Alam II granted the Company the diwani in 1765.

places.name: Faizabad
places.why: The capital of Awadh under Shuja-ud-Daula.

places.name: Shahjahanabad (Delhi)
places.why: The Mughal capital. Nadir Shah sacked it in 1739, the year before this period begins.

places.name: Panipat
places.why: In 1761 Ahmad Shah Durrani crushed the Marathas here. The defeat left a power vacuum in the north that the Company would later fill.

places.name: Madras
places.why: Fort St George, the Company's Coromandel base. The French held it from 1746 to 1749.

control.note: Returned under the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle

places.name: Fort St David
places.why: The Company's southern fort. Clive served here in the 1740s.

places.name: Pondicherry
places.why: Capital of French India. The British took it in 1761, and France got it back in 1765.

control.note: Returned after the Treaty of Paris (1763)

places.name: Goa
places.why: Capital of the Portuguese Estado da Índia since 1510.

places.name: Bombay
places.why: Came to the Company in 1668 and became its western headquarters.

places.name: Surat
places.why: The great Mughal port of the west coast. The English and Dutch had factories here.

places.name: Masulipatnam
places.why: A textile port on the Coromandel coast. The French held it in the 1750s, and Forde took it in 1759.

places.name: Arcot
places.why: Capital of the Nawabs of the Carnatic. Clive's defence of the fort in 1751 made his name.

places.name: Wandiwash
places.why: Site of the 1760 battle that ended serious French hopes of an empire in India.

events.name: Battle of Giria
events.summary: Alivardi Khan, deputy governor of Bihar, kills Nawab Sarfaraz Khan and takes the throne of Bengal.
events.why: It starts the reign that Siraj-ud-Daulah would inherit. It is also a usurpation, so the Mughal emperor's approval was something bought rather than something that mattered.

events.name: Maratha raids on Bengal
events.summary: Bhonsle cavalry, known as bargis, raid western Bengal again and again for a decade. Bengali poetry remembers widespread killing, plunder and refugees fleeing east across the Bhagirathi.
events.why: The raids weakened Bengal's countryside and finances. They also pushed merchants and weavers to move under the protection of Company-held Calcutta.

events.name: Orissa ceded to the Marathas
events.summary: Alivardi Khan buys peace by ceding Orissa and promising annual chauth (a tribute) for Bengal.

events.name: Siege of Arcot
events.summary: Clive takes Arcot with a small force and holds it through a 50-day siege. The aim was to draw pressure away from the British-backed claimant, Muhammad Ali, at Trichinopoly.
events.why: The siege made Clive famous and showed that small, well-drilled forces could decide Indian wars.

events.name: Siraj-ud-Daulah becomes Nawab
events.summary: Alivardi Khan dies, and his grandson Siraj-ud-Daulah, about 23 years old, succeeds him.

events.name: Kasimbazar factory seized
events.summary: Angry that the Company was fortifying Calcutta without permission and sheltering his enemies, Siraj-ud-Daulah seizes the English factory at Kasimbazar.

events.name: Fall of Calcutta
events.summary: The Nawab's army takes Fort William. The governor and most of the Council escape downriver to Fulta. The city is renamed Alinagar.

events.name: Black Hole of Calcutta
events.summary: British prisoners are held overnight in the fort's small lock-up, and many die. The main account is by survivor J. Z. Holwell.
events.why: The numbers are disputed. Holwell's figures were later used as justification for empire, and modern historians treat them with caution.

figures.label: Prisoners confined
figures.note: Holwell gave 146. Later research estimates about 64.

figures.label: Deaths
figures.note: Holwell gave 123. Later research estimates about 43.

events.name: Battle of Manihari
events.summary: Siraj-ud-Daulah defeats and kills his cousin and rival Shaukat Jang of Purnea.

events.name: Calcutta retaken
events.summary: A relief force from Madras under Clive and Admiral Watson retakes Fort William with little resistance.

events.name: Treaty of Alinagar
events.summary: After an indecisive clash at Calcutta, the Nawab restores the Company's privileges and allows it to fortify Calcutta.

events.name: Capture of Chandernagore
events.summary: With the Seven Years' War under way in Europe, the British attack and capture the French settlement upriver.
events.why: It removed the Nawab's only possible European ally in Bengal.

events.name: Battle of Plassey
events.summary: About 3,000 Company troops face the Nawab's army of about 50,000. Before the battle, Clive had agreed with the Nawab's commander Mir Jafar and the Jagat Seth bankers that Mir Jafar would replace Siraj-ud-Daulah. Mir Jafar's large division stays out of the fight. A rainstorm soaks the Nawab's gunpowder, and the Nawab's army breaks.
events.why: Plassey was a battle decided by bribery and a coup. It made the Company the power behind the throne of the richest province in India.

figures.label: Company force
figures.note: About a third European, two-thirds Indian sepoys

figures.label: Nawab's force
figures.note: Estimates vary widely, and a large part never engaged

events.name: Mir Jafar made Nawab
events.summary: Clive installs Mir Jafar at Murshidabad. Mir Jafar pays the Company and its officers vast sums, which empties the treasury.

events.name: Siraj-ud-Daulah killed
events.summary: Siraj-ud-Daulah is captured while fleeing and executed on the orders of Mir Jafar's son, Miran.

events.name: 24 Parganas granted to the Company
events.summary: The Company receives the zamindari of the lands south of Calcutta: its first territory in Bengal.

events.name: Battle of Chinsurah
events.summary: A Dutch force sent from Batavia is defeated near Chinsurah. This ends Dutch ambitions in Bengal.

events.name: Battle of Wandiwash
events.summary: Eyre Coote defeats Lally's French army in the Carnatic. Pondicherry is besieged soon after.
events.why: This was the decisive battle in the struggle between the British and the French in India.

events.name: Mir Qasim replaces Mir Jafar
events.summary: The Company replaces the bankrupt Mir Jafar with his son-in-law Mir Qasim, who cedes Burdwan, Midnapore and Chittagong.

events.name: Third Battle of Panipat
events.summary: Ahmad Shah Durrani destroys the Maratha army north of Delhi. It was one of the largest battles of the 18th century.
events.why: It checked Maratha expansion in the north for a decade, just as the Company was rising in the east.

events.name: Fall of Pondicherry
events.summary: The French capital surrenders after a long siege.

events.name: Battle of Udhwa Nala
events.summary: Mir Qasim had tried to end the Company's tax-free private trade, and war followed. The Company storms his fortified line, and he flees west to Awadh.

events.name: Battle of Buxar
events.summary: Hector Munro's Company army defeats the combined forces of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula of Awadh and the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II.
events.why: Unlike Plassey, this was a hard-fought battle against the leading powers of the north. It was won on the field, and it settled who ruled eastern India.

events.name: Treaty of Allahabad
events.summary: Shah Alam II grants the Company the diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa, in return for a pension and the districts of Allahabad and Kora. Awadh is restored to Shuja-ud-Daula for an indemnity.
events.why: The trading company became the legal revenue authority of tens of millions of people. Many historians date the start of British rule in India to this treaty.

people.name: Robert Clive
people.role: Company soldier and Governor of Bengal
people.summary: A Company clerk turned soldier. He made his name at Arcot, won Plassey through a planned defection, and as governor obtained the diwani at Allahabad. He returned to Britain enormously rich, and Parliament investigated him.

perspectives.text: The founder of British India, a bold commander who saw a political opportunity and took it.
A man who conquered by bribery and coup, and whose regime in Bengal led to plunder and the famine of 1770.

itinerary.note: Takes a commission in the Company army
Returns as governor of Fort St David
Sails with Watson's fleet for Bengal
Leaves India for the last time

people.name: Siraj-ud-Daulah
people.summary: The last independent Nawab of Bengal. He moved quickly against the Company's unauthorised fortification of Calcutta, but he alienated the bankers and nobles at his own court. They then conspired with Clive.

perspectives.text: Portrayed as a cruel and reckless young tyrant, an image built largely on Holwell's Black Hole narrative.
A patriot who defended Bengal's sovereignty and was betrayed by Mir Jafar. "Mir Jafar" became a byword for traitor.
An inexperienced ruler with real grievances against the Company, undone by a court coalition of bankers and generals who wanted him gone.

people.name: Alivardi Khan
people.summary: A soldier from Bihar who seized Bengal at Giria. He spent much of his reign fighting off Maratha raids.

people.name: Mir Jafar
people.summary: Siraj-ud-Daulah's commander. He held back his troops at Plassey and was made Nawab in return. The Company deposed him in 1760 and restored him in 1763.

people.name: Mir Qasim
people.summary: An able administrator who reformed revenue and moved his capital to Monghyr. He went to war when he tried to curb the Company's abuse of tax-free trade.

people.name: Shuja-ud-Daula
people.summary: Led the largest army at Buxar. After defeat, he kept Awadh in exchange for an indemnity.

people.name: Shah Alam II
people.summary: An emperor without a capital in the 1760s. At Allahabad he granted the Company the diwani in return for a pension.

people.name: Hector Munro
people.summary: Commanded the Company army at Buxar.

stories.title: Plassey to Buxar
stories.subtitle: How a trading company took Bengal, 1740–1765

steps.title: A province worth an empire
steps.text: In 1740 Bengal is the richest province of the Mughal Empire, in practice independent under its Nawab at Murshidabad. Europeans trade along the Hooghly at its edge: English at Calcutta, Dutch at Chinsurah, French at Chandernagore.

steps.title: The bargis
steps.text: For a decade Maratha cavalry from Nagpur raid western Bengal. In 1751 Alivardi Khan buys peace by giving up Orissa. Watch it change colour.

steps.title: Orissa lost
steps.text: Orissa passes to the Bhonsles of Nagpur. Meanwhile, in the south, a young Company clerk named Robert Clive has just held Arcot against a siege.

steps.title: Alinagar
steps.text: The new Nawab, Siraj-ud-Daulah, objects to the Company fortifying Calcutta without his permission. He marches south and takes the city. The night of the "Black Hole" follows, and its numbers are still disputed.

steps.title: The relief from Madras
steps.text: Clive and Admiral Watson sail north from Madras and retake Calcutta in January 1757.

steps.title: Plassey
steps.text: A mango grove on the Bhagirathi. The deal was struck before the battle: the commander Mir Jafar stays out of the fight, and the Nawab's army breaks.

steps.title: The first territory
steps.text: The Company's reward includes the zamindari of the 24 Parganas, its first block of territory in Bengal. More follows in 1760 when Mir Qasim is made Nawab.

steps.title: Two decisive defeats
steps.text: In the same week the Marathas are crushed at Panipat and Pondicherry falls to the British. The Company's two great rivals, the Marathas in the north and the French in the south, are both checked.

steps.title: Buxar
steps.text: Mir Qasim, the Nawab of Awadh and the Mughal emperor combine against the Company, and they lose. Unlike Plassey, this is a real battle.

steps.title: The diwani
steps.text: At Allahabad the emperor grants the Company the diwani, the right to collect the revenue of Bengal, Bihar and Orissa. A trading company is now a government.
